# Legacy source checkpoints

These four manually authored legacy-LIA profiles cover straight return,
if/else, early-return/fallthrough and ordered guarded scalar match with a
wildcard. The frozen source hashes, exact path conditions, return substitutions
and command sequences are trusted reviewed inputs, not a compiler-generated
source inventory. The descriptor review is technical and carries no human or
organizational independence claim.

The checker must authenticate source-bound signed replay with the caller-pinned
compiler and solver before comparing structure. Only lexical parallel-let
expansion is permitted. Guard order, connective/assertion multiplicity and
return-expression structure remain exact. Equivalent `x + 0` and extra `true`
axiom mutations are checkpoint-policy deviations, not numerical unsoundness.
The four separate wrong-return sources supply feasible source counterexamples.

This legacy subset neither reinterprets the separate BV expectations nor
includes the pending typed-try inventory/precision gates preserved in draft
#5015. It does not establish automatic source enumeration, arbitrary source
translation correctness, machine arithmetic qualification or external acceptance.
Public test records are bounded to256KiB each; that bounds emitted records,
not compiler subprocess execution/output. Executable identities do not establish
complete dynamic linkage or whole-environment identity.

The first-match descriptor is now checkpoint revision2. Its exact variadic
`and`/`or` print shape was manually reviewed against source after hosted capture
40073120470; pre-capture exact-serialization provenance does not apply to this
revision. Revision1 bytes and their earlier source-review hashes remain in
`first_match_checkpoint_revision1.json`; the revision2 review records both
hashes and the original failure. The checker still performs no Boolean
flattening or equivalence normalization.
